messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: The luteal phase starts 14 days before the period is due.
The luteal phase continues until the period starts.
This process is repeated with each cycle.
On daily dosing, the dose can go up by 50 mg per cycle.
The maximum dose is 150 mg a day.
On luteal phase dosing, the maximum is 100 mg a day.
The dose is taken as 50 mg for the first 3 days of the dosing cycle.
The dose is 100 mg for the rest of the cycle.
Sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules.
These are not used to start treatment.
They are not used to titrate a dose.
This is because there are no lower capsule strengths.
They can be started in someone who has been taking 100 mg or 125 mg of another sertraline product for at least a week.
The recommended capsule dose is 150 mg or 200 mg once a day.
The maximum dose is 200 mg a day.
Coming off treatment requires switching back to another sertraline product.
This is because the dose cannot be lowered in steps using capsules alone.
Liver problems.
Sertraline is available in tablet and oral solution forms.
Mild liver impairment is defined as a Child-Pugh score of 5 or 6.
Triples: [["luteal phase", "starts", "14 days before the period is due"], ["luteal phase", "continues until", "the period starts"], ["this process", "is repeated with", "each cycle"], ["on daily dosing", "has dose increase", "50 mg per cycle"], ["maximum dose", "is", "150 mg a day"], ["on luteal phase dosing", "has maximum dose", "100 mg a day"], ["the dose", "is taken as", "50 mg for the first 3 days of the dosing cycle"], ["the dose", "is", "100 mg for the rest of the cycle"], ["sertraline", "has dosage form", "150 mg capsule"], ["sertraline", "has dosage form", "200 mg capsule"], ["these", "are not used to start", "treatment"], ["these", "are not used to", "titrate a dose"], ["these", "can be started in someone who has been taking", "100 mg or 125 mg of another sertraline product for at least a week"], ["recommended capsule dose", "is", "150 mg or 200 mg once a day"], ["maximum dose", "is", "200 mg a day"], ["coming off treatment", "requires switching back to", "another sertraline product"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "liver problems"], ["sertraline", "has dosage form", "tablet"], ["sertraline", "has dosage form", "oral solution"], ["mild liver impairment", "is defined as", "child-pugh score of 5 or 6"]]
Relations: ["are not used to", "are not used to start", "can be started in someone who has been taking", "continues until", "has dosage form", "has dose increase", "has maximum dose", "has side effect", "is", "is defined as", "is repeated with", "is taken as", "requires switching back to", "starts"]
Answer:

completion:
are not used to: The subject entity is not used for the action or purpose specified by the object entity.  
are not used to start: The subject entity is not used to initiate or begin the process specified by the object entity.  
can be started in someone who has been taking: The subject entity can be initiated in a person who has been using the dosage or product specified by the object entity.  
continues until: The subject process or phase continues until the event or condition specified by the object entity occurs.  
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.  
has dose increase: The subject dosing regimen allows for an increase in dose by the amount specified by the object entity.  
has maximum dose: The subject dosing regimen has a maximum dose specified by the object entity.  
has side effect: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or complication specified by the object entity.  
is: The subject entity is defined or described by the object entity.  
is defined as: The subject condition or term is defined by the specific criteria or value specified by the object entity.  
is repeated with: The subject process or cycle is repeated with the frequency or interval specified by the object entity.  
is taken as: The subject dose or regimen is administered in the specific form or amount specified by the object entity.  
requires switching back to: The subject process or action requires the transition or change to the product or regimen specified by the object entity.  
starts: The subject process or phase begins at the time or condition specified by the object entity.
